user_prompt: Write a reply to my landlord disputing the $75 late fee. Mention Section 4.2 and the grace period. Keep it under 120 words.
final_prompt:
Write a reply to my landlord disputing the $75 late fee. Mention Section 4.2 and the grace period. Keep it under 120 words.

<document>
From: Dana Whitfield, Maple Court Apartments
Subject: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi,

Our records show this month's rent was received on the 3rd. As you know, rent is due
on the 1st, so a late fee of $75 has been added to your account. We were disappointed
to see this, since on-time payments help us keep the building running for everyone.
We'd appreciate it if you could be more careful going forward. Please pay the fee
along with next month's rent.

Thanks for understanding,
Dana

---
Lease excerpt (Maple Court residential lease):
Section 4.1: Rent is $1,450 per month, payable by check, money order, or the resident
portal.
Section 4.2: Rent is due on the 1st. A grace period applies through the 5th; no late
fees may be charged during the grace period.
Section 4.3: Returned payments incur a $35 fee.
Section 9.4: Notices to the landlord must be in writing and may be sent by email.
</document>

Subject: Dispute of Late Fee - Unit 3B

Hi Dana,

Thank you for your message. I'm writing to dispute the $75 late fee added to my account for this month.

Per Section 4.2 of the Maple Court residential lease, rent is due on the 1st, and a grace period applies through the 5th. The lease states that no late fees may be charged during the grace period. My rent was received on the 3rd, which falls within that grace period, so the fee does not comply with the lease terms.

I'd appreciate it if you could reverse the $75 charge and update my account accordingly. Please confirm once this has been corrected.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Best regards,
[Your name]
Unit 3B
[Date]

---

Before sending, you may want to check your payment records to confirm the date the payment was received, and keep a copy of this email along with the lease for your files. If the fee isn't reversed, you could follow up in writing, and if needed, consult your local tenant rights organization or housing authority about your options.
